thread:
Jordan (support): FYI customer (acct: acme-inc) reports tool call failing with a 400. They pasted the args from a Word doc. Error: "tool args invalid JSON". Ticket: https://zendesk.example/12345

Jordan (support): Their raw arg string (copied):
```json
{"path": \u201cC:\\Users\\Bob\\Documents\\Project\\file.txt\u201d,}
```

Jordan (support): Note the trailing comma and the left/right smart quotes around the path. They said it used to work earlier this week.

Maria (support): Can you repro? if it's smart-quotes + trailing comma we should return a clearer error and a KB entry.

Ingrid (eng): Repro'd quickly. Parser throws a 400 with our generic message. Log excerpt:
```
ERROR inference-parser: invalid JSON at byte 14: invalid character '\u201c' looking for beginning of value
request_id=req_01G1234Z
```

Ingrid (eng): TL;DR: Word/Slack paste sometimes turns straight quotes into U+201C/U+201D. Also trailing comma makes it invalid for strict JSON. Minimal repro curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"tool":"read_file","args":"{\"path\": \u201cC:\\\\tmp\\\\x.txt\u201d",}'}'
```

Ingrid (eng): Fix options:
- sanitize incoming args string (normalize smart quotes to ASCII quotes, strip trailing commas) before parse (fast patch)
- improve parser error message to include byte offset and suggest 'check for smart quotes / trailing comma' (UX)
- update SDK to run a preflight check and surface a better error client-side

Maria (support): Customer is blocked on automation. Can we do the "fast patch" server-side today? They cannot change their client.

Ingrid (eng): I can push a small sanitizer in the toolcall entrypoint that normalizes common unicode quotation marks and runs a tiny trailing-comma stripper. Will open PR. It should be safe for 99% of cases.

Ingrid (eng): Quick patch notes (will PR after tests):
```py
# naive sanitizer
def sanitize_tool_args(s):
    s = s.replace('\u201c','\"').replace('\u201d','\"')
    s = re.sub(r',\s*}\s*$', '}', s)
    return s
```

Jordan (support): Awesome. Please include a log flag so we can see when sanitizer ran (so we can tell customer we fixed).

Ingrid (eng): Will add `sanitizer=smartquotes` audit field to request logs. Also adding a unit test for a few paste variants.
